subject: Autoscaler lag causing sustained tail-latency | Ops update & mitigation plan
messages:
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@cartwheel.ai>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 5 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production errors: high tail latency + intermittent 503s on dedicated pool

Sean —

We started seeing a sustained increase in tail latency for our dedicated pool (region: us-west-2) around 08:50 PDT. Several inferences returned 503s and a lot of requests are hitting 500–700ms tail latency (usually < 120ms). This is impacting our real-time recommendation path.

Attached are a few request traces and a small sample of errors (error-samples.log). We also noticed a pattern where requests routed to pool-rt-07 are disproportionately affected — tracer IDs start with rt:7.

Can you confirm if this is a platform issue or something on our side? We’re on a tight release window today.

—Alex

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 5 Oct 2028 12:20:45 -0700
Subject: Internal: initial triage — autoscaler contention + allocator backlog

Sean / Laura — internal notes (please keep Alex informed with the high-level items only). Quoting the customer’s report below.

On Fri, 5 Oct 2028 at 09:12, Alex Torres <alex.torres@cartwheel.ai> wrote:
> We started seeing a sustained increase in tail latency ...

Findings (initial):
- Symptoms: elevated tail latency and intermittent 503s across a subset of nodes (pool-rt-07).
- Root cause (suspected): our autoscaler’s allocation worker experienced a mutex contention combined with slow heartbeat responses from the allocator service. This created a backlog of scale decisions and delayed new instance attachments for a ~7 minute window starting ~08:48 PDT. The backlog increased request queuing on a limited set of warm nodes causing head-room exhaustion and subsequent 503s.
- Contributing factor: a recent change to KV-cache eviction heuristics (deployed 10/04) increased cache miss amplification under certain traffic patterns; that amplified per-request compute and extended the time nodes stayed hot.

Short-term mitigations applied (10:05–12:05):
1) Manual scale-up: provisioned 4 warm nodes into reserved pool-rt-07 to relieve headroom pressure (impact: immediate tail latency reduction on sample traces).
2) Fail-open routing: temporarily routed new requests for Cartwheel AI to spare nodes in us-west-2 while allocator backlog drained (impact: stabilized success rate).
3) Autoscaler patch: deployed a lock contention fix to allocation worker to reduce queuing delays (hotfix id: INF-9921).

Next actions (owner):
- Evelyn: complete root cause analysis and validate hotfix across canary tenants by EOD.
- Laura: coordinate customer communications + credit offer.
- Sean: confirm customer acceptance of fallback routing and get any additional traces.

We should follow up with a formal postmortem once we have full logs and metrics. I’ll attach allocator heartbeats and a brief timeline in the postmortem doc.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Director, Infrastructure Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@cartwheel.ai>
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 6 Oct 2028 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Mitigation complete — steps taken, next steps, and credit offer

Alex —

Thanks again for flagging this. Quick summary and next steps: 

What happened (high level)
- Between ~08:48–08:55 PDT on 2028-10-05 our autoscaler experienced lock contention that delayed allocation decisions for pool-rt-07. That backlog led to queuing on warm nodes and a spike in tail latency / 503s for a subset of your traffic. A KV-cache eviction heuristic change on 10/04 increased cache-miss amplification and lengthened warm node residency which made the pool more sensitive to the autoscaler delay.

What we did
- Applied manual scale-up to add 4 warm nodes to the affected pool and performed fail-open routing to spare nodes (10:05–10:20 PDT).
- Deployed a targeted autoscaler hotfix (INF-9921) that removes the contention point in the allocation worker (10:33 PDT).
- Rolled back the KV-cache eviction change for affected model families as a precaution (11:05 PDT).

Impact now
- Observed tail latency returned to baseline across your traces and 503 counts dropped to normal. We’ll keep monitoring for 48 hours and will reach out immediately if we see regressions.

Follow-ups & customer support
- We will deliver a formal postmortem to you by 2028-10-09 with full timelines, root cause data, and a remediation plan to prevent recurrence.
- As a goodwill gesture we’ll issue a service credit for the partial degradation window; Laura will follow up with the credit amount and paperwork.
- Attached is an ops-runbook excerpt describing the autoscaler safeguards we’ll add to your tenant (ops-runbook-v2.pdf).

If you’re available, I’d like to set a 30-minute post-incident review with your SREs on Tue 10/09 at 10:00 PDT to walk through the postmortem and recommended tenant-level settings (conservative batching / prefork headroom).

Apologies again for the impact — we understand how time-sensitive this is.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

(attachments: ops-runbook-v2.pdf)
